Shifted slices and results of `_SPMDInternalOp_MultiSlice` custom calls are handled through a `SliceDesc` abstraction that describes a slice either as an instruction or as one result of a multislice. `IsSliceExpansionCommunicationFree` reports whether a leaf is aligned with the window on every partitioned dimension; the expansion is only used if at least one leaf is communication-free.

The duplicated slice-and-reshard logic in `ProcessUpdatePieceExtractOperand` is factored into a `SliceUpdatePieceSource` helper, which also keeps that function under the 500-line lint limit.

Adds four partitioner tests: elementwise over aligned slices, shifted slices, multislice results, and slice-plus-constant.

display_title: PR #51992: [XLA:TSL] Check output buffer capacity in SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate

head_commit.message:
PR #51992: [XLA:TSL] Check output buffer capacity in SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51992

#ai-generated

**Status quo:** `SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate` checks the uncompressed block size against its output buffer with `DCHECK_GE` (`xla/tsl/lib/io/snappy/snappy_inputbuffer.cc:131`).

**Why:** The check disappears in release builds, so `Snappy_Uncompress` can write a block larger than `output_buffer_capacity_` into the output buffer.

**Design choices:** Return `absl::ResourceExhaustedError` before decompression when the block exceeds the configured capacity, with the same message format as `SnappyInputStream::Inflate` and the input buffer capacity check above it. A valid block can exceed a caller's configured capacity, so this is a sizing error rather than data loss. Add GoogleTest coverage for an exact fit, spare capacity, and rejection when capacity is insufficient. The successful cases also exercise multiple blocks and reset.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives:** Keep the existing fixed buffer capacity instead of allocating based on the input block. This change is confined to Snappy input buffering.

**Testing:** `bazel test //xla/tsl/lib/io/snappy:snappy_test` passes (12 of 12 tests) on Linux x86_64 with `-c opt` and with AddressSanitizer. Without the `snappy_inputbuffer.cc` change, `UncompressedBlockExceedsOutputBuffer` fails in the `-c opt` build because `Inflate` returns OK, and the AddressSanitizer build reports a heap-buffer-overflow write in the Snappy decoder called from `SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate`.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Allow runtime DUS start indices on non-partitioned dims in the constant-index handler (Enzyme opt)

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Allow runtime DUS start indices on non-partitioned dims in the constant-index handler (Enzyme opt)

With `xla_enable_enzyme_comms_opt`, `AnalyzeDynamicUpdateSlice` routed a dynamic-update-slice to `HandleDUSAllPartitionedSliceDimsHaveConstantIndices` only if every start index was a constant. This change relaxes that:

* A runtime start on a dimension that is *not* partitioned is fine: every shard holds that dimension in full, so the handler cuts the update region out of the local shard with a `dynamic-slice`, applies the (constant-offset) update pieces inside that region via `ProcessUpdatePiece` with a new `region_shape` parameter, and puts the region back with a local `dynamic-update-slice`. No all-gather is needed.
* A size-1 update with a runtime start on a *partitioned* dimension now correctly reports `has_partitioned_slice_dim_with_dynamic_index` (which partition it lands in is only known at runtime), so it takes the single-partition path instead of the constant-index one.
* Full-size slices (update dim == operand dim) always start at 0, so their start index is ignored regardless of whether it is constant.

Adds three partitioner tests covering these cases.

Ported from https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/blob/main/patches/xla_dus_dynamic_index.patch

display_title: [XLA] CollectivePermuteCSE: merge permutes of overlapping/adjacent windows of one array

head_commit.message:
[XLA] CollectivePermuteCSE: merge permutes of overlapping/adjacent windows of one array

Previously `CollectivePermuteCSE` only deduplicated collective-permutes whose operands were identical, or where one operand was a single slice directly of the other's operand.

This change generalizes the pass to reason about the *window* each permute's operand reads from a root array, resolved through a chain of unit-stride slices:

* Two permutes (with equal `source_target_pairs`) whose windows of the same root are nested reuse the larger permute; the smaller one becomes a slice of it. This now works through arbitrarily deep slice chains (`slice(slice(p0))`), not just a single slice.
* Two permutes whose windows differ in exactly one dimension with touching or overlapping intervals are replaced by a single permute of their union window. The union moves no element that neither original permute moved. Both originals (and any unit-stride slices of them left by earlier unions) become slices of the union permute, so a chain of adjacent windows collapses into one permute (see `ThreeWindowsUnion`).

Control dependencies of the merged permutes are transferred to the union permute, skipping predecessors reachable from either original to avoid cycles.

Windows that are disjoint, differ in more than one dimension, have different `source_target_pairs`, or go through strided slices are left alone.

Ported from https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/blob/main/patches/xla_collective_permute_cse_windows.patch

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/xla/third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch
Why needed: Replaces entry_map_.find(key) on std::multimap with entry_map_.lower_bound(key) in @onednn_async (v3.12.3), @onednn_async_aarch64, and @mkl_dnn_acl_compatible (v3.11.3) so eltwise_injector iterates over all matching entries under C++20 libc++ (fixing the segfault in //tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl:mkl_fused_ops_test).

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

display_title: Preserve narrow-float values across identity reduce-precision in XLA.

head_commit.message:
Preserve narrow-float values across identity reduce-precision in XLA.

`jax.checkpoint` (remat) pins saved floating-point residuals that are also read in the forward pass with `reduce-precision` set to the element type's own exponent and mantissa bit widths so that excess-precision optimizations cannot give the forward and backward passes different values. For 8-bit and 4-bit floating-point types, `FloatNormalization` previously promoted an identity `reduce-precision` to a wider floating-point type (`f16` or `f32`), turning it into a non-identity IEEE-style bit-fiddle with infinities and without subnormals (for example, corrupting `f8e4m3fn` values in 256..448 to `NaN` and flushing subnormals to zero). `HloEvaluator` and the MLIR and LLVM emitters had the same issue when lowering identity `reduce-precision` ops.

Add `primitive_util::HasFloatingPointPrecision` and treat `reduce-precision` instructions whose `exponent_bits` and `mantissa_bits` match their element type's bit widths as supported in low precision in `FloatSupport`, without allowing `--xla_allow_excess_precision` to elide the low-precision conversion feeding them. Short-circuit identity `reduce-precision` in `HloEvaluator`, `EmitReducePrecisionIR` (also replacing `nbits - 1 - src_mantissa_bits` with `primitive_util::ExponentWidth(src_ty)` because `F8E8M0FNU` has no sign bit), and `mapMhloOpToStdScalarOp` (fixing the off-by-one in `HasDefaultMantissaBits` and `HasDefaultExponentBits`, where `mlir::FloatType::getFPMantissaWidth()` includes the implicit leading bit and unsigned float types such as `Float8E8M0FNUType` have no sign bit via `llvm::APFloat::semanticsHasSignedRepr`).

Preserve narrow-float values across identity reduce-precision in XLA.

`jax.checkpoint` (remat) pins saved floating-point residuals that are also read in the forward pass with `reduce-precision` set to the element type's own exponent and mantissa bit widths so that excess-precision optimizations cannot give the forward and backward passes different values. For 8-bit and 4-bit floating-point types, `FloatNormalization` previously promoted an identity `reduce-precision` to a wider floating-point type (`f16` or `f32`), turning it into a non-identity IEEE-style bit-fiddle with infinities and without subnormals (for example, corrupting `f8e4m3fn` values in 256..448 to `NaN` and flushing subnormals to zero). `HloEvaluator` and the MLIR and LLVM emitters had the same issue when lowering identity `reduce-precision` ops.

Add `primitive_util::HasFloatingPointPrecision` and treat `reduce-precision` instructions whose `exponent_bits` and `mantissa_bits` match their element type's bit widths as supported in low precision in `FloatSupport`, without allowing `--xla_allow_excess_precision` to elide the low-precision conversion feeding them. Short-circuit identity `reduce-precision` in `HloEvaluator`, `EmitReducePrecisionIR` (also replacing `nbits - 1 - src_mantissa_bits` with `primitive_util::ExponentWidth(src_ty)` because `F8E8M0FNU` has no sign bit), and `mapMhloOpToStdScalarOp` (fixing the off-by-one in `HasDefaultMantissaBits` and `HasDefaultExponentBits`, where `mlir::FloatType::getFPMantissaWidth()` includes the implicit leading bit and unsigned float types such as `Float8E8M0FNUType` have no sign bit via `llvm::APFloat::semanticsHasSignedRepr`).

display_title: [XLA] CollectivePermuteCSE: merge permutes of overlapping/adjacent windows of one array

head_commit.message:
[XLA] CollectivePermuteCSE: merge permutes of overlapping/adjacent windows of one array

Previously `CollectivePermuteCSE` only deduplicated collective-permutes whose operands were identical, or where one operand was a single slice directly of the other's operand.

This change generalizes the pass to reason about the *window* each permute's operand reads from a root array, resolved through a chain of unit-stride slices:

* Two permutes (with equal `source_target_pairs`) whose windows of the same root are nested reuse the larger permute; the smaller one becomes a slice of it. This now works through arbitrarily deep slice chains (`slice(slice(p0))`), not just a single slice.
* Two permutes whose windows differ in exactly one dimension with touching or overlapping intervals are replaced by a single permute of their union window. The union moves no element that neither original permute moved. Both originals (and any unit-stride slices of them left by earlier unions) become slices of the union permute, so a chain of adjacent windows collapses into one permute (see `ThreeWindowsUnion`).

Control dependencies of the merged permutes are transferred to the union permute, skipping predecessors reachable from either original to avoid cycles.

Windows that are disjoint, differ in more than one dimension, have different `source_target_pairs`, or go through strided slices are left alone.

Ported from https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/blob/main/patches/xla_collective_permute_cse_windows.patch

[TSL:CUDA] Demote missing CUDA drivers message to VLOG(1) in cudart_stub

On systems without CUDA drivers (e.g. CPU-only workstations or containers), attempting to dynamically load the CUDA runtime DSO fails as expected. Demoting this log to VLOG(1) prevents unwanted STDERR noise on default verbosity while retaining diagnostic output when verbosity is explicitly requested (e.g. via TF_CPP_MAX_VLOG_LEVEL=1).

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

display_title: Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

head_commit.message:
Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

When a second client connects to an IFRT proxy server that only supports a single active client, the server terminates the session with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Only one client can connect via the proxy server at a time.`. Previously, `GrpcClientSession` could overwrite this status with `CANCELLED` (by calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` even when `ReadLoop()` had already exited) or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (if `Finish()` completed before `Enqueue()`).

Avoid calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` when `ReadLoop()` has already exited, and store the final session status in `finish_status_` so subsequent `Enqueue()` calls return it.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013156692

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleDynamicSlice`
(`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), folding a
1D `dynamic-slice` of an `iota` (or scaled `iota`) clamps the scalar
`S32`/`U32` start index to `[0, iota_size - 1]` by narrowing
`iota_size - 1` directly to `int32_t` or `uint32_t`. When
`iota_size - 1` exceeds `INT32_MAX` (for `S32` indices) or `UINT32_MAX`
(for `U32` indices), the upper bound wraps around and corrupts the
clamped index.

Saturate the clamp upper bound to the maximum representable value of
`index_type`, which is equivalent across all 32-bit index values, and
add symbolic >32-bit `S32` and `U32` unit tests.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012198883

display_title: Support cross-memory-kind donation and mark donated buffers deleted in PjRtArray.

head_commit.message:
Support cross-memory-kind donation and mark donated buffers deleted in PjRtArray.

Previously, `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` rejected `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` when copying across different memory kinds with an `Unimplemented` error, left the source array's `PjRtBuffer` pointer intact when donating on the same device and memory kind, and did not call `PjRtBuffer::Delete()` on the source buffer when donating across devices or memory spaces. In addition, several `PjRtArray` methods assumed elements of `pjrt_buffers_` were non-null even after cross-device donation set `pjrt_buffers_[index] = nullptr`.

Allow `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` across different memory spaces in `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` by deleting and clearing the source `PjRtBuffer` after `CopyToMemorySpace` initiates the transfer, and move `pjrt_buffers_[index]` when donating on the same device and memory kind so the source `PjRtArray` is marked deleted. Guard against null donated buffer slots in `CopySinglePjRtBuffer`, `CopyImpl`, `CopyToHostBuffer`, `GetReadyFuture`, and debug checks in `pjrt_layout`.

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.
Copybara import of the project:

--
9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

--
305022f3c7322f0cd593997b81715ea9ed473d15 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Bail out of the trivial reduce-window rewrite for any dynamic operand with a crop

The slice that applies a negative window padding covers every dimension of
the operand, so a dynamic dimension without a crop still breaks it. Check the
whole operand shape once before slicing instead of only the cropped dimension.

Merging this change closes #48875

display_title: Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

head_commit.message:
Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

When `PjRtCApiCompiler::Compile` is called for ahead-of-time compilation without a live `PjRtClient` (`client == nullptr`), `SerializeProgram` previously could not query `client->plugin_attributes()` and fell back to the default 12-week compatibility StableHLO and Shardy versions (`xla::GetDefaultStablehloVersion()` and `xla::GetDefaultSdyVersion()`).

Because `PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` is a plugin-level C API call on `const PJRT_Api*` that does not require a `PJRT_Client*`, fall back to querying `c_api->PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` when `client == nullptr` (or when the client does not report attributes) so ahead-of-time compilation serializes programs using the plugin's actual `stablehlo_current_version` and `sdy_current_version`.

display_title: Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

head_commit.message:
Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

When a second client connects to an IFRT proxy server that only supports a single active client, the server terminates the session with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Only one client can connect via the proxy server at a time.`. Previously, `GrpcClientSession` could overwrite this status with `CANCELLED` (by calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` even when `ReadLoop()` had already exited) or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (if `Finish()` completed before `Enqueue()`).

Avoid calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` when `ReadLoop()` has already exited, and store the final session status in `finish_status_` so subsequent `Enqueue()` calls return it.

display_title: Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

Dispatching executables with thousands of outputs currently calls `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` and `GetOnDeviceBytesCount` once per non-aliased output leaf, while `use_output_arena` couples all output buffer lifetimes to the longest-lived output buffer.

Add `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` (with a default implementation delegating to `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` so existing backends such as GPU and CPU preserve their current behavior), cache static output leaf buffer sizes in `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::output_buffer_sizes_in_bytes_`, and dispatch one `AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` call per memory space in `CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` when `use_output_arena` is disabled.

display_title: Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

`CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` currently scans `device->memory_spaces()` on every non-aliased output leaf, allocates non-arena buffers inline during the loop, and collects arena allocations into an unordered pointer-keyed `absl::flat_hash_map<PjRtMemorySpace*, ...>`. Preparing for per-memory-space batched output allocation requires deterministic grouping of pending output allocations across both the default and arena paths.

Collect non-aliased output allocations into an `absl::InlinedVector` ordered deterministically by first-seen memory space `kind_id`, resolving `PjRtMemorySpace*` once per distinct `kind_id`, and execute either the per-output or arena allocation loop over those grouped entries with no functional change.

Enable multi-subscriber graph trace attribute for CUPTI V2 graph-level tracing.

When CUPTI V2 multi-subscriber mode (`allowMultipleSubscribers = 1`) is active (such as in CUDA 13.4 static CUPTI builds), enabling `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` via `cuptiActivityEnable_v2` returns `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` unless the global `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_MULTI_SUBSCRIBER_GRAPH_TRACE` (`20`) attribute is set to `1` before enabling any activity kinds.

display_title: [PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

head_commit.message:
[PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

When executing CPU computations, PJRT and XLA thread pools configure the CPU to flush subnormal floating-point numbers to zero to improve performance. However, when XLA calls back into Python (via `jax.pure_callback`, `io_callback`, or `buffer_callback`), this setting was left enabled on the calling thread. Python code (like NumPy) expects standard floating-point behavior, so leaving this setting enabled caused subnormal numbers to silently become zero inside user callbacks.

This change adds `tsl::port::ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and `tsl::port::ScopedSetRound(FE_TONEAREST)` to `xla::HostCallbackScope`. This ensures all Python callbacks run with standard floating-point settings, and safely restores XLA's expected settings when the callback returns.

Bumps `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 84 and adds regression tests guarded by this version.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012993070

head_commit.message:
PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

🎯 Justification
`ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper` creates async computations on the parallel execution thread, while `SanitizeConstantNames` previously ran only on the main execution thread.

As a result, constants in these async computations could reach GPU code generation with unsanitized names and trigger the ConstantNameToGlobalName DCHECK.

This change runs constant-name sanitization across all execution threads while keeping the remaining post-scheduling passes scoped to the main execution thread.

Fixes #50829

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
NA

🧪 Unit Tests:
Added `GpuCompilerTest.SanitizesConstantNamesInParallelExecutionThread`, which compiles an HLO containing a constant inside a stream-annotated call through the GPU compiler pipeline.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No execution tests added.

display_title: Fix 32-bit overflows in SPMD pad-with-wrap and iota partitioning

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit overflows in SPMD pad-with-wrap and iota partitioning

Fix three >32-bit dimension bugs in `xla/service/spmd/spmd_partitioner.cc`:
1. In `SpmdPartitioner::PreprocessHlos`, widen `rotate_lhs_amount` from `int`
   to `int64_t` and use `U64` (instead of `U32`) for the merge `iota` and
   `select` limit constants when `padded_size > UINT32_MAX`.
2. When `padded_size > INT32_MAX`, guard the pad-with-wrap rewrite on matching
   even shardings for `mid` and `hlo` and bounded halo size so uneven sharding
   or large halos fall back to standard `kConcatenate` partitioning instead of
   hitting 32-bit helpers.
3. In `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleIota`, compute shard offsets in 64-bit
   (`U64` for `U64` iota, `S64` otherwise) whenever `shard_dim > INT32_MAX` or
   `(num_shards - 1) * shard_dim > INT32_MAX`, preserving the `S32` path for
   smaller shapes.

display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on `multiProcessorCount`, so aot plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we plumb the compile-time `GpuTargetConfig` from `GpuExecutable` (`gpu_topology_`) into `Thunk::InitializeParams`, extract the target SM count in `CuDnnThunk`, and pass it to `DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`. When that target SM count is lower than the attached GPU's, `CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` builds `DeviceProperties` from the live `DeviceDescription` with `core_count` lowered to match (keeping all other hardware properties from the live GPU for validation) and runs warmup on the handle.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013012065

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` multiplied the per-tile coalescing
utilization rate by the transfer-size HBM derate on dot fusions, compounding
both penalties on small GEMMs into an unrealistically low effective bandwidth.
Take the minimum of the two rates instead and apply it in floating point.

In addition, when a fused prologue widens narrow inputs (such as `s8 -> bf16`),
counting only fusion parameter reads under-estimates K-loop L2 traffic by 2x
and causes slow widening fusions to beat cuBLASLt. Bound L2 traffic below by
the masked dot-operand tile reads across the K-loop.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000319647

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011625424

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `HloModule*` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (or with `embed_hlo_module = false`) do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013010631

- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CUDNN_FISSION autotuner backend for scaled dots.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDNN_FISSION autotuner backend for scaled dots.

Problem:    cuDNN swizzles scaled dot scales in place, after fusion.
Solution:   Autotune cuDNN on GEMM fusions with a CUDNN_FISSION backend.

CUDNN_FISSION runs CudnnScaledDotRewriter on the unfused GEMM fusion, so
the scale padding and swizzle fuse with the scale producers. It races Triton
and CUBLASLT_FISSION and tunes all cuDNN plans. CudnnBackend now accepts only
cuDNN fusions that CudnnScaledDotRewriter built. TritonBackend and
FissionBackend do not retune them.

display_title: [XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleDynamicSlice`
(`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), folding a
1D `dynamic-slice` of an `iota` (or scaled `iota`) clamps the scalar
`S32`/`U32` start index to `[0, iota_size - 1]` by narrowing
`iota_size - 1` directly to `int32_t` or `uint32_t`. When
`iota_size - 1` exceeds `INT32_MAX` (for `S32` indices) or `UINT32_MAX`
(for `U32` indices), the upper bound wraps around and corrupts the
clamped index.

Saturate the clamp upper bound to the maximum representable value of
`index_type`, which is equivalent across all 32-bit index values, and
add symbolic >32-bit `S32` and `U32` unit tests.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `HloModule*` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (or with `embed_hlo_module = false`) do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

head_commit.message:
Skip unaffected JAX CI builds using Bazel query

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

Dependent small fusions are often dominated by fixed kernel launch and scheduling overheads when run as separate kernels. Executing dependent fusions as sequential phases of a single Hopper (SM90+) thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers pays that launch overhead only once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches. Note that `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` (cl/1012181303) combines independent fusions across disjoint CTAs and is complementary.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Only straight-line chains of `kLoop` fusions
* Nested fusion must fit a single thread block cluster
* No buffer aliasing with fusion outputs

head_commit.message:
Split Starlark `= rule(...)` declarations out of `lit.bzl` and `tools/source_hash.bzl` into separate private `.bzl` files (`lit_rules.bzl` and `tools/source_hash_rules.bzl`).

Motivation: In Bazel, a `.bzl` file that defines a `= rule(...)` pulls the transitive closure of its `load()` statements into the dependency graph of every target instantiating that rule. Moving rule declarations to dedicated `.bzl` files avoids unnecessary downstream target invalidation when macro-only `.bzl` dependencies change.

Testing: Verified affected build and test targets and Starlark parse tests.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Re-record command buffers when symmetric memories change.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Re-record command buffers when symmetric memories change.

Even though currently thunks are not using symmetric memories directly in the kernels in theory it's possible through FFI (see relevant collective ops ffi test). Therefore once collective memory is re-created a corresponding graphs should be re-captured. Note that this change will detect only change of symmetrical memories associated to the collective memory space. If FFI thunk allocates its own symmetrical memories -- they won't be detected.

To detect this we give every `SymmetricMemory` a process-unique id that is never reused.
`CommandBufferThunk` remembers, per device, the (key, id) pairs of the symmetric
memories its command buffer was recorded with
(`CollectiveMemory::symmetric_memory_ids()`), compares them exactly and without
allocating against the current `CollectiveMemory` on every execution, and
replaces the command buffer with a new one when they differ.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012959203

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `HloModule*` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (or with `embed_hlo_module = false`) do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011555676

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012829918

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CUDNN_FISSION autotuner backend for scaled dots.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDNN_FISSION autotuner backend for scaled dots.

Problem:    cuDNN swizzles scaled dot scales in place, after fusion.
Solution:   Autotune cuDNN on GEMM fusions with a CUDNN_FISSION backend.

CUDNN_FISSION runs CudnnScaledDotRewriter on the unfused GEMM fusion, so
the scale padding and swizzle fuse with the scale producers. It races Triton
and CUBLASLT_FISSION and tunes all cuDNN plans. CudnnBackend now accepts only
cuDNN fusions that CudnnScaledDotRewriter built. TritonBackend and
FissionBackend do not retune them.

Reverts c6f5a2f70ed039969bc985c8aab989e783c203b3

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011625424

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `HloModule*` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (or with `embed_hlo_module = false`) do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

head_commit.message:
PR #52112: XLA: Treat empty tuple sharding as non-single-device

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52112

📝 Summary of Changes
Modified HloSharding::IsSingleDevice() to return false for an empty tuple.

🎯 Justification
An empty tuple sharding {} has no unique device, but `IsSingleDevice()` previously returned true because `absl::c_all_of()` returns true for an empty range.

This caused `HandleCustomCall()` to route a ()-shaped custom call to `HandleSingleDevice()`, which calls `GetUniqueDevice()` and aborts because no unique device exists.

The change makes `IsSingleDevice()` consistent for empty tuple shardings.

Resolves #51433

NA

Updated `hlo_sharding_test.cc` to verify that an empty tuple sharding with no sharding elements is not considered single-device.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No Execution tests were added.

display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

name: CI
display_title: Verify that all processes compiled the same executable

head_commit.message:
Verify that all processes compiled the same executable

If the processes of a multi-process run compile different executables, they can issue collectives in a different order and hang until some timeout kicks in. One way to get there is autotuning with `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false`, since then each process autotunes on its own and can end up with a different schedule.

So this change makes `FunctionalHloRunner::Compile` publish the fingerprint of the compiled executable in the key-value store and compare it with the fingerprints of all other processes. If they differ, compilation fails with a `FailedPrecondition` error that lists which processes compiled which fingerprint. The check only runs if the compile options contain a key-value store and more than one process.

The fingerprint covers the optimized HLO including the schedule, but not backend configs. So it catches a different order of collectives, but not every difference in the autotuning results. (For GPU the fingerprint gets computed during compilation anyway, so the check is cheap.)

The check is on by default, which means that runs where the processes compiled different executables but happened not to hang will fail now too. I think that's the better default since the processes don't run the same program in that case. The check can be disabled with `PreprocessingOptions::verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` or the `--verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` flag of `//xla/tools/multihost_hlo_runner:hlo_runner_main`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012914882

name: CI
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Evict command buffers when a GPU clique is split or destroyed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Evict command buffers when a GPU clique is split or destroyed.

When a cached GPU clique is abandoned during communicator splitting or
destroyed, any command buffers recorded with resources tied to that clique
become stale. Tie per-clique cleanup state (`CliqueState`) to each acquired
clique via `CollectiveCliques::TieAll(...)` when the command buffer is created.
When any of those cliques are abandoned or destroyed, `~CliqueState()` resets
the command buffer on that device, ensuring stale CUDA graphs are cleaned up
before `ncclCommDestroy` runs and forcing re-capture on the next execution.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `const HloModule&` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) when `options.embed_hlo_module && !options.early_exit_with_layouts`, and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` and `GpuCompilerTest.DoesNotUploadSymbolsWhenUnembedded` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (such as `EarlyExitPoint::kAfterLayoutAssignment`) or with `embed_hlo_module = false` do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

name: CI
display_title: Verify that all processes compiled the same executable

head_commit.message:
Verify that all processes compiled the same executable

If the processes of a multi-process run compile different executables, they can issue collectives in a different order and hang until some timeout kicks in. One way to get there is autotuning with `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false`, since then each process autotunes on its own and can end up with a different schedule.

So this change makes `FunctionalHloRunner::Compile` publish the fingerprint of the compiled executable in the key-value store and compare it with the fingerprints of all other processes. If they differ, compilation fails with a `FailedPrecondition` error that lists which processes compiled which fingerprint. The check only runs if the compile options contain a key-value store and more than one process.

The fingerprint covers the optimized HLO including the schedule, but not backend configs. So it catches a different order of collectives, but not every difference in the autotuning results. (For GPU the fingerprint gets computed during compilation anyway, so the check is cheap.)

The check is on by default, which means that runs where the processes compiled different executables but happened not to hang will fail now too. I think that's the better default since the processes don't run the same program in that case. The check can be disabled with `PreprocessingOptions::verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` or the `--verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` flag of `//xla/tools/multihost_hlo_runner:hlo_runner_main`.

display_title: [NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

head_commit.message:
[NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

`BufferAllocation` is used by runtime targets that only need allocation metadata and slices, so it shouldn't depend on `HloValue` (which pulls in `hlo/ir:hlo`).

We move the per-allocation `HloValue` state and heap traces into a parallel `allocation_values_` vector in `BufferAssignment` (indexed by `BufferAllocation::index()`) and remove the `HloValue` accessors from `BufferAllocation`.

We keep serializing `assigned` inside `BufferAllocationProto` (populated by `BufferAssignment::ToProto()`, while standalone `BufferAllocation::ToProto()` leaves it empty) rather than moving it onto `BufferAssignmentProto` for now. Several `HloProto` consumers (e.g. XProf and `ComputePeakMemorySizes`) read `BufferAllocationProto.assigned` directly instead of going through `BufferAssignment::FromProto()`. Switching the writer right away would also break CPU/GPU AOT forward compatibility when older readers load new protos, so moving the proto field would require a multi-stage rollout across repos.

A follow up CL will actually split the files

name: CI
display_title: Fix oneDNN batched matmul data race for K >= 20000 on CPU

head_commit.message:
Fix oneDNN batched matmul data race for K >= 20000

In oneDNN's CPU brgemm_matmul primitive, k-partitioning reduction was enabled
for huge K (K >= 20000) and small M/N (<= 512) without checking that batch == 1.
Because the parallel reduction logic and scratchpad buffer in brgemm_matmul
hardcode batch index 0 for reduction buffers and output pointers, concurrent
execution with batch > 1 caused data races, non-deterministic outputs, and
massive numerical errors.

This patch restricts use_k_partitioning to batch == 1, matching the existing
guards on all other k-partitioning paths in brgemm_matmul_utils.cpp.

Fixes https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/129498

name: CI
display_title: Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

head_commit.message:
Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

`Executable` takes its `HloModule` in the constructor and never changes it.
But we want `GpuExecutable` to build its module from a serialized module only
when something needs it (e.g. the profiler), and once that happened the module
should be visible through `has_module()`, `module()` and `shared_module()` like
any other module.

So this change adds a second `Executable` constructor that takes an
`HloModuleFactory` instead of a module, and `Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule`,
which returns the module and builds it with the factory if needed. The factory
is called at most once, even with concurrent callers, and if it fails every
later call returns the same error. After a successful build `has_module()`
returns true. The accessors do an acquire load of a raw pointer to the module
and only look at the `shared_ptr` once that pointer is non-null (it never
changes after that), so the read path doesn't need a lock. (We can't use
`std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>` since XLA still has to build with C++17.)

The lazy state lives in a separate heap allocation, so executables that get
their module in the constructor don't pay for it and behave exactly as before.
There is also a new `Executable(std::nullptr_t)` constructor, since
`Executable(nullptr)` would be ambiguous otherwise.

Convolution canonicalization skips the `xla_gpu_enable_fast_min_max` setting, leaving NaN propagation enabled even when fast min/max is requested. Apply the same setting here as in the other GPU algebraic simplifier modes. The default behavior is unchanged.

A focused regression test checks the existing min/max infinity rewrites with the flag on and off, for both CUDA and non-CUDA options.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Evict command buffers when a GPU clique is split or destroyed.

When a cached GPU clique is abandoned during communicator splitting or
destroyed, any command buffers recorded with resources tied to that clique
become stale. Tie per-clique cleanup state (`CliqueState`) to each acquired
clique via `CollectiveCliques::TieAll(...)` when the command buffer is created.
When any of those cliques are abandoned or destroyed, `~CliqueState()` resets
the command buffer on that device, ensuring stale CUDA graphs are cleaned up
before `ncclCommDestroy` runs and forcing re-capture on the next execution.

name: CI
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012088899

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.
